title: How BAD is Hamza's Fitness Advice? (5 BIGGEST Reasons You Can't Gain Muscle)
summary: NH reviews Hamza's video on why you can't gain muscle. He agrees with the anti-maingaining and nuanced bulking points, flags the low-testosterone focus, and rejects the one-set intensity experiment, the no-pain-no-gain framing and the claim that 10-15 reps is best and you should never go below 8. NH recommends 6-15 reps.
claims: Agrees: skinny guys afraid of gaining weight waste years; you must gain weight to gain muscle
Maingaining is promoted because 'gain muscle and lose fat at once' is attractive, often by enhanced people, and it left many young men with no results
Even for a six-pack you must build the abdominal muscles first, then get lean
Plenty of channels, including NH, have warned against maingaining; it is not the mainstream view Hamza implies
Choose the eating mode that suits your situation; NH has recomped for three years and it worked because he had enough fat
Setting a target body weight (Hamza: 180 lb) and gaining toward it without stuffing your face is good nuanced advice; NH dirty-bulked and just got fat
Calories are not equal in food quality; fitness channels have said this for years
Blaming low testosterone for poor gains is a trend that masculinity gurus exploit; beware anyone selling test boosters or seminars
Fix lifestyle (training, diet, sleep, hobbies) and testosterone takes care of itself; young men jumping to TRT without fixing lifestyle is the dumbest move
Microplastics are not responsible for your small biceps; the environment you choose is
The one-set experiment fails: set one is the same whether three sets follow or not; if you get more reps, you were sandbagging out of psychology
One set of 17 reps cannot beat four sets with 13 on the first and 10+ on each of the others; the extra sets add 30+ reps
The HIT idea that extra sets take away from the first set is an anachronistic view of training
If you can psych up two more reps after 'failure', the earlier reps were not 100% effort
No-pain-no-gain is a male power fantasy; there is no logical link between pain felt and hypertrophy
Intensity is a number, the load relative to your max; screaming and grinding high-rep sets is mostly pump theatrics
You can gain muscle with sub-par sleep, but sleep matters for mood, hormones, and reducing Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and heart disease risk
NH admits he sometimes skimps on sleep to make an extra video; the grindset hurts vitality
Agrees: pick an exercise and rep range and progress within it, rather than chasing a target weight
Saying 10-15 is the best hypertrophy range and never go below 8 is wrong and leads to plateaus
If you can grind 2 more reps past 'failure' at 15 reps, the load is not challenging the muscle
6-10 reps are more intense than 10-15 because they use heavier relevant loads and reach true mechanical failure
Singles, doubles and triples are useless for hypertrophy if they make up most of your training; most work should be in the 6-15 range
Focusing only on reps eventually stops working, just as focusing only on bar weight does; use both
Two weeks is not enough to see visible muscle change from a rep-range switch; the rep range is a parameter for progression, not progression itself
Prefer advice from people with more experience; recommends Alpha Destiny, Geoffrey Verity Schofield, Bald Omni Man and Basement Bodybuilding
